svg.text: Longitudinal section (schematic, not to scale). One cell = a rounded-rectangular capsule bored into a wall, with a single piston that slides along it.
Piston shown DEPLOYED (cell open, in use). To close, the piston travels toward the street until its own face is the flush public wall.
ServiceSqueegee travels the sealed chamber — stows behind the piston ▸

g.text: A–A (capsule cross-section)
flat floor
width 1000 · height 1100
corner R 125 (mm)
crown light (6)
B–B (service side — two chain lanes)
central = piston chain · +Y = squeegee chain + yoke
shared bore, no wall slot (ADR-0021)

svg.text: Key dims (mm): cavity length 2200 · width 1000 · height 1100 · wall 6 · piston length 300 · running clearance 3 (seals bridge it) · install depth ≈ 2940 (2.94 m) · mouth sill ≈ 500 above ground

g.text: 1 · CapsuleShell (fixed barrel)
The stationary sleeve. The occupant lies inside it; the piston slides
through it. Open at both ends (street opening + service side).
2 · Piston — the ONE moving part
Its flat face is the occupant's backrest when open, and becomes the
flush public wall when closed. No separate door. (ADR-0001)
3 · WiperSeals (safety fn SF3)
Compliant lip rings on the piston. Fill the 3 mm gap so there is no
open shear line, and scrape the bore clean each pass. (ADR-0011)
4 · Chain drive: Column + Magazine
Pushes/pulls the piston. The chain coils flat into the magazine so the
unit stays ~2.9 m deep, not ~5 m. (ADR-0008 / 0010)
5 · Return spring + flush latch (SF4)
Fail-open: on power loss the spring drives the cell OPEN so no one is
pinned; a passive latch holds it shut without power. (ADR-0009)
6 · Luminaire (ADR-0014)
Warm, dim, flicker-free strip flush in the crown. Orientation light,
sleep-safe night-glow, and status colour. Cleaned by the top wiper.
7 · Occupancy sensors (SF1, ADR-0012)
Diverse suite — radar vitals + thermal + CO₂ + load. The primary
safeguard: the cell NEVER moves while anyone/anything is inside.
8 · Safety edge (SF2)
Contact-force strip on the leading face. Stops and reverses the close
on any touch — the backstop behind SF1.
9 · Mouth sill (~500 mm, ADR-0013)
Sitting-height lip at the opening, so items swept out fall clear onto
the tray instead of jamming the sill.
SF = a rated safety function; ADR = a logged design
decision in docs/DECISIONS.md.
10 · SprayRing (front)
Nozzle ring just PAST the closed piston — sprays the sealed chamber's
front + rinses the piston face in transit (detergent → hot water → disinf.).
11 · ServiceSprayRing (deep, hidden)
A 2nd ring behind the deployed piston face — never seen by the user;
washes the chamber's far end when the cell is closed.
12 · SumpDrain — wash-media drain
Hot water + chemicals → sewer, hidden UNDER the piston when deployed.
Never a grate in the occupied cavity or on the public face.
13 · TrenchDrain
Flush pavement grate at the mouth; catches ejected SOLIDS + rain →
sewer. Serviced from below.
14 · ServicePlant
Back-of-house box: hot-water/steam gen, disinfectant + doser, dry-air
blower, pump.
15 · ServiceSqueegee (traveling wiper)
Runs the full sealed chamber while the piston is parked flush — a car
wash over the stopped piston; scrubs + drives media to the sump. Hidden.
16 · SqueegeeDrive
The squeegee's OWN compact rigid-chain — a modular, bench-testable,
swappable unit nested beside the piston's actuator. No added depth.
17 · SqueegeeChain + Yoke (coupling, ADR-0021)
The drive's chain runs in an OFFSET +Y lane INSIDE the sealed bore; a short
yoke couples it to the centered ring — no wall slot. Works because the piston
(central) and squeegee (offset) never share the chamber at once. See B–B.
ADR-0015–0021: nothing on the public face; two rings + a traveling
squeegee (its own drive) wash the sealed chamber; media to the hidden sump.
